1.why: Four options are logistics (made in town, fits the case, gift not loan, trade taught); E alone states a provenance principle, and item 15 refers to 'the rule that produced it', so the passage needs a rule with consequences.

2.why: Only option stating a principle rather than a logistic of winding - the other four are arrangements, C is the thematic line.

3.why: Only two-part option (claim X is false AND a smaller claim is available) among four single propositions - the thesis shape.

4.why: Item 9's distractor E mentions 'the thickness of the varnish on the lower half of the board', so varnish is in the passage; C is the varnish option.

5.why: D is the scold-the-institution option and B is generic background; E is the thematic-loss summary that item 25's 'will not find them under that name' echoes.

6.why: Item 20B (the mussels occupy only the stretch that got both changes) makes attribution impossible, so the stance is sure of the decline and silent on cause.

7.why: The passage is the slate-dressers' tools (items 1/5/25), so 'dressed' means worked a hard material to shape.

8.why: An ink passage (13/14/19/21), so 'body' is thickness and substance, not torso or text.

9.why: Given item 4 makes the board unreadable, the narrative-mechanism option that sends Nance back to the unread part is the one that does work in the scene.

10.why: Ferry passage, so 'draws' is the boat sense - needs a stated depth of water to float.

11.why: Item 3D says a smaller claim that will stand is available instead; the deed's own date is that claim, which requires the deed to postdate the printed one.

12.why: The only option that supports the decline the passage asserts - a size distribution missing young mussels is recruitment failure.

13.why: B and C are the same mechanism in two wordings and cancel; of the rest, D is the only one turning on the varnish that item 19C makes the firm's own.

14.why: The qualified hedge that commits to interest and withholds a verdict, with the reason named (one line of a day-book); A/D are the doubly-committed pair and E the indifference bait.

15.why: D/E are a minimal pair differing on one clause, and item 1 states the rule as still in force, so the key is the side that keeps it.

16.why: Item 28B reports the fall shortened by seven feet, which is the answer to E's question - the two items are a matched question and finding.

17.why: Clock passage (2/16/24/28), so 'going' is the running of a machine.

18.why: B/D are a minimal pair on the second clause; a scene whose point is the miller's motive (item 27) turns on Nance revising her reading, not confirming it.

19.why: Item 14 puts a day-book entry in evidence, which implies a bought pigment and kills D ('never committed to paper'); C is the shop-made option consistent with a purchase record.

20.why: The only option that is a true confound - one stretch receiving both changes - rather than a dating or provenance quibble.

21.why: Only option covering both halves the passage demonstrably has (survival, item 13; origin, item 19); the others each name one strand.

22.why: Item 3D makes the target the printed claim, not the family, so the stance is friendly with the impatience aimed at the wrapper.

23.why: Item 6 names the farm and the dredging as the two candidates; B is the only pair containing both.

24.why: Item 2C argues that a hand-wound clock dies with its winder, which is an argument against Marr's refusal rule, so the anecdote is the rule failing.

25.why: Pairs with item 5E ('what was lost'): the loss is findability under the wrong name, not physical access or doubt about Cudworth.

26.why: Mussel passage (6/12/20/23), so 'bed' is the ground lying under a stream.

27.why: If item 18 turns on Nance revising her reading of the miller, the true motive must be the generous one she had not credited.

28.why: Item 16E asks whether the weights still have their built fall; B is the finding that answers it, and the other four are parish logistics.

29.why: Item 3D says a smaller claim that will stand is offered instead, so the pivot is the writer turning from demolition to a claim he will defend.

30.why: Item 3A fixes the stone as chapel-cut, narrowing to A/B; B is the version a document could witness, which item 29A ('a witness not called earlier') wants.
